title: UX patterns
summary: Checkout, forms, search, filters, lists, and mobile patterns from Baymard’s free research.

overview.purpose: Before finishing a flow, check it against these patterns.
overview.when: A form, checkout, search, or list is built and you need the pattern that fails.
takeaways: Show the full cost before payment
Keep labels and what people typed
Say what went wrong and how to fix it
Show filters, suggestions, and list facts

sections.title: Patterns
sections.intro: Before finishing a flow, check it against these patterns. For each one that fails, name the screen, the problem, and the fix.

items.title: Field labels
items.fix: The label disappears as you type, so keep it above the field.
items.why: Baymard’s checkout research says the label should stay visible while people type, especially on mobile.

items.title: Form length
items.fix: The form is longer than the job, so cut the default checkout toward 12 to 14 elements.
items.why: The average US checkout shows 23.48 form elements. Testing found an ideal flow can be as short as 12 to 14.

items.title: Guest checkout
items.fix: It looks like you must register, so put Guest Checkout first, as a button.
items.why: 18% of surveyed US adults had abandoned an order in the previous three months because they were forced to create an account.

items.title: Total cost
items.fix: It hides the total, so show shipping, tax, and the full cost before payment.
items.why: 12% of surveyed US online shoppers have abandoned an order because they could not see the total cost up front.

items.title: Card number
items.fix: The card number is one long string, so space it like the card and check it as they type.
items.why: Baymard’s checkout research says to auto-format spaces and use a Luhn check so a typo is caught while the card is in hand.

items.title: Error messages
items.fix: The error just says invalid, so say what is wrong and how to fix it, next to the field.
items.why: 98% of sites don’t say exactly what is wrong and how to fix it. Keep what the person already typed.

items.title: Search suggestions
items.fix: The search box is a dead end, so suggest queries as they type.
items.why: Baymard finds autocomplete works best when it suggests queries, not only products, and stays short enough to scan.

items.title: Applied filters
items.fix: The filters vanish after you pick them, so show each one as a chip you can remove.
items.why: 20% of ecommerce sites fail to keep applied filters visible.

items.title: Filter choices
items.fix: It lets you pick only one, so let people select several options in the same filter.
items.why: 14% of sites don’t let users select more than one option in a filter, and testing showed people then abandon products.

items.title: Main navigation
items.fix: The menu hides the catalog, so put product categories on the first level.
items.why: Baymard’s navigation testing found that hiding categories behind one item such as “Products” makes the site hard to browse.

items.title: Product lists
items.fix: The list is only pictures, so show the price and the facts people compare on each card.
items.why: Baymard’s product-list research says the list should carry price and the attributes people use to compare, not only a thumbnail.

items.title: Mobile filters
items.fix: Filters eat the screen, so open them from a sticky Filter button and confirm with Show results.
items.why: On mobile, Baymard recommends a drawer, a Filter button that stays put, and a Show results action.
